lesson_title: Motion Graphs: The Drawing That Does Your Physics
hook_text: No formulas. One drawing. The whole journey — accelerations AND 550 metres — read straight off it.
clip_script: Draw the taxi trip as a velocity-time graph: a ramp climbing to 20 metres per second, a plateau, a steep ramp back to zero. Now read it. Steepness is acceleration: the climb rises 20 in 10 — that is 2 metres per second squared. The plateau is level — zero. The fall drops 20 in 5 — minus 4. And the area underneath is distance: a triangle, half of 10 times 20 — 100 metres. A rectangle, 20 times 20 — 400. A last triangle — 50. Total: 550 metres. Two accelerations and the whole distance, from one silhouette and primary-school geometry. That is why the velocity-time graph is the best deal in Grade 10 physics.
visual_style: A mountain-silhouette graph draws itself; steepness values pop off each slope, then the shape floods with colour as triangle-rectangle-triangle areas count up to 550.
pacing: Silhouette drawn fast, gradient reads snap in, area flood builds to the 550 reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read a driver's foot straight off a graph.
